notes.title: Crimson Tactics Retrospective
notes.content:
It’s coming up to a year since we launched Crimson Tactics: The Rise of The White Banner and we would like to take a moment to retrospect the development of our first title. We are also eternally grateful to all the players that tried our game despite its many glaring faults. 

We would like to give a brief overview of what really happened. This is the story from our perspective.

[h2]Development[/h2]

Crimson Tactics was our studios’ first title. We are based in India, a country where you can count the number of shipped PC/Console Games on both hands (as of writing this). Needless to say, pretty much everyone on the team was new to developing these kinds of games. To say that we did not know what we were doing would be an understatement. We were pretty much figuring stuff out as we go in regards to both development and production. This led to a massive over-scoping of this project and our inexperience led us to underestimate the time required to ship all the features.

We want to stress that we are not some high profile developer with years of experience under our belt. Pretty much everyone on our team was new to this.

This resulted in us taking too long to launch the game into Early Access. We had to delay the game thrice because it was not ready. Moreover, the systems in the game were developed in a very amateurish and inefficient manner which led to a huge problem that comes into context a bit later.

[h2]What Happened at EA Launch[/h2]

On the launch day of Early Access (25th July, 2023), we were actually getting positive reviews for the game but the sales were extremely weak. We had also exhausted most of our funds trying to push the game into Early Access as we had to delay the game thrice to get it to a polished state. The poor sales and low remaining funds put us in a pretty bad spot after the launch.

Over the month of July, we waited to see if sales would improve but to no vail and after evaluating the situation in August, we realized that we had the funds to run the studio at its current state for just 1 more month.

[h2]Early Access Content[/h2]

Early Access was essentially Feature Complete. What that means is that all the features we hoped to have in the final game were already complete. What remained was adding additional Story and Gameplay Content.

Early Access launched with the following things:

- 10+ Classes.
- 75+ Abilities.
- 3+ Mounts.
- 25+ Hour Story Campaign.
- 30+ Levels.

In our Early Access messaging, we were very clear and said that we planned the following things for Full Release:

- 20+ Classes.
- 200+ Special Abilities.
- 5+ Mounts.
- 50+ Hour Story Campaign.
- 75+ Levels.

Moreover, we planned to gradually increase the price of the game (from $30 to $40).

This information can be found on this [url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230720151843/https://store.steampowered.com/app/1480810/Crimson_Tactics_The_Rise_of_The_White_Banner/]Web Archive Page[/url].

This snapshot was taken on 20th July, 2023, 5 days before our Early Access Release and has the most up to date information up to that point in time.

In our messaging, we stress that we have [b]planned[/b] the things and we [b]hope[/b] to develop these things. 

Internally, these were just rough plans that we hoped to realize during Early Access. Nothing more than Early Access content was even conceptualized up until then.

We were naïve and inexperienced. In our understanding, plans are not hard promises and hoping to develop something is not a hardened promise of delivery.

We never thought that these plans and hopes would be interpreted as hard bound promises that we absolutely must deliver on. This led to a lot of misinformation and baseless accusations being spread on the Steam Forums. We will be much more careful moving forward on how we communicate our plans and promises.

[h2]Post Early Access[/h2]

After Early Access Launch, the game was actually getting positive reviews but the sales were extremely poor. And as mentioned before, we had about 1 month of runway left for the team.

Instead of abandoning the game at Early Access and letting it stay in Early Access forever, we decided to get as much work done as possible and push for a Full Release.

Since Early Access was already Feature Complete, we decided that the best we could do was:

- 15+ Classes.
- 150+ Abilities.
- 5+ Mounts.
- 40+ Hour Story Campaign.
- 50+ Levels.

in the month of time we had left.

We worked hard to get this done and released the Full Release on 5th September, 2023. We did the best we could with the resources we had left.

[h2]Communication Woes[/h2]

Behind the scenes, things were hectic as we worked hard to get the things done for Full Release. We got accused of lying and communicating our new plans just 1 day before release. 

Heck, even we were not sure what we could get done in that short period of time for Full Release. We had already failed on delivering our plans once.

And yes, we handled communications for this title in a very amateurish manner which could have been handled much better. We apologize for this and we will strive to do better next time.

[h2]Post Full Release[/h2]

Needless to say, people were not satisfied with our Full Release as the reviews turned from Mostly Positive to Mixed and justifiably so. 

Revenue from the game did not improve and there was no way to keep the same team and we had to disband.

We got in touch with all our industry contacts to see if anyone was hiring and fortunately, a lot of studios were. Thankfully, we managed to get most developers a new job at other studios.

[h2]State of Crimson Tactics[/h2]

The game is complete from our end. We have implemented what we could for this game and have pushed out a Full Release.

We understand that it’s not perfect and the story ends very very abruptly but we are also getting feedback that the game is fun though mounts are useless.

We actually agree with most of the recent feedback we are getting on the game.

A lot of users are asking why can’t we just develop this game further and make this game better?

The reason is quite simple. Due to our inexperience, the game was developed in an extremely inefficient manner. This was highlighted earlier. Making just one change to a system can cause multiple other systems to come toppling down. Our Technical Debt is really high. This funny comic elucidates this further:

[img]https://pbs.twimg.com/media/EVv1DH9WoAEpvAA?format=jpg[/img]

Moreover, pretty much all the original developers of Crimson Tactics have left Black March Studios to work elsewhere and it’s pretty much impossible for a new developer to comprehend the mess that is Crimson Tactics’ codebase.

[h2]What’s Next?[/h2]

If you are a customer of Crimson Tactics and feel hoodwinked by our first title where we faltered heavily, we understand and apologize profusely. 

If this experience makes you never want to try any of our future games, we completely understand and again apologize profusely for making you experience this.

That said, we plan to keep making more games. Now we know what to do and what not to do. We refuse to let one setback disrupt our dreams and ambitions.

As for the future of Crimson Tactics, we are not quite sure. Given sufficient interest, we might consider making a sequel. We still want to make more tactics games in general even if they are not related to Crimson Tactics.

Thanks again,
Black March Studio

notes.title: Full Release Announcement
notes.content:
Crimson Tactics: The Rise of The White Banner is out now on Full Release. Please check out the launch trailer:

[previewyoutube=mal0ApRKU58;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]Full Release Content[/h1]
Over the Early Access Period, the game went through major revisions and polishes, and the story was expanded and made complete. We are launching the full game with the following content:
[list]
[*] 40 Hour+ Story Campaign.
[*] 15+ Playable Classes.
[*] 3+ Playable Mounts.
[*] 50+ Playable Levels.
[/list]

[h1]Early Access Feedback and Changes[/h1]
Early Access was essentially released as Feature Complete. That said, it was instrumental in polishing and tweaking the game. The following things were changed and tweaked based on Early Access Feedback:
[list]
[*] RNG was severely tweaked and fixed.
[*] Game Speed was significantly increased. The current 3x speed is as fast as the backend system will allow the game to go.
[*] Prologue was made skippable.
[*] Classes were balanced and tweaked.
[*] A lot of small UI fixes.
[*] Controller and Steam Deck support was introduced.
[*] Tweaks to the various AI profiles.
[*] Rogue AI was reworked to Pilfer more stuff.
[*] Ability to name generic units was introduced.
[*] Autosave before battle puts you back on the world map.
[*] Re-balanced and Tweaked the Crafting System.
[*] Experience and SP Systems were re-balanced and tweaked for both units and mounts.
[*] Automatic Difficulty System was balanced and smoothened.
[*] Weather and Lightning Systems were tweaked.
[/list]

Moreover, we fixed each and every single bug that was reported by the Early Access players both in the Steam Forums and in our Discord Server.

[h1]Post Release Support and QoL Polish[/h1]
With the Full Release, we are marking the game as both Feature and Content Complete. The game is essentially done. That said, if any new bugs are discovered after Full Release, we will fix them ASAP and push out a patch.

Moreover, we will continue to polish the game with small QoL changes and features based on further feedback. While we don't plan to introduce any big features, these will be small things that will make the game's experience a little bit more pleasant.

notes.title: Crimson Tactics Devlog #093
notes.content:
Swordmaster specializes in close-quarters combat. They are typically characterized by their high attack power, speed, and pinpoint high accuracy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/8eb9c3a5900030b54cb6e138ba65c67f58206f58.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/35ec657f775d3440940999ea81cf4baf49bf182e.png[/img]

[h2]Sword Dances[/h2]

Swordmasters can deal a significant amount of damage to the enemies along with applying a number of debuffs with their Sword Dances, making them a very demanding class.

[h3]Serpent Dance[/h3]

The unit performs a Sword Dance, stunning the target and preventing them from moving. This can be used to trap targets in one place.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/954f8f5d1b352567201309def1e3692a15005173.gif[/img]

[h3]Demon Dance[/h3]

The unit's deadly Sword Dance that can leave its target bleeding out, slowly but surely draining their health.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/12c219c9505b2514636ae4f97fdebe0bbc183170.gif[/img]

[h3]Frost Dance[/h3]

The unit's Sword Dance ability freezes the target, preventing them from taking any actions for a few turns.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/ec60b5aa51828c154442f07368ef29cce92220a6.gif[/img]

notes.title: Crimson Tactics Devlog #092
notes.content:
Ninja acts as an agile and stealthy class that brings a new dimension to combat, allowing players to infiltrate the enemy lines and take them down from behind.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/74b3be71376ab4a4b2b217d0d680afef8ea091ea.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/79082752fbc83426bed9fdcb56e257fec3d35b01.png[/img]

[h2]Special Abilities[/h2]

Ninjas can deal with the enemies in the stealthiest way possible which makes them a great support unit at your disposal.

[h3]Substitution Jutsu[/h3]

The unit trades places with an ally unit to take advantage of their superior position or might also offer them protection.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/77d6e8587661b89e42a109969e9855a0f5eefd0d.gif[/img]

[h3]Seduction Jutsu[/h3]

The unit is a master of persuasion, and they can convince even the most hardened enemy to join their cause.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/b455ee4b8bfab2fb3d79ed8714284f2bf35aaabc.gif[/img]

[h3]Kitsune Jutsu[/h3]

The unit transfers all the status effects to the target unit, be it a buff or a debuff.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/c6109136dc07faf01f9b64bf3b3e35c8df837e32.gif[/img]

These changes will be introduced in the next patch based on your valuable feedback!

We've heard your feedback, and we're excited to announce that you'll now be able to rename your generic units in Party Management. This was a popular request from Early Access players, and we're excited to see how you use it!

Increasing the game’s speed and pacing was a highly requested feature during our previous beta. Hotkeys functionality has been added to the game and is also reflected in the UI. We plan on expanding this feature further but in its current state, it is greatly improving the game’s flow.

[h2]Action Panel Hotkeys[/h2]

The Action Panel can now be accessed with Hotkeys. The numbers on the keyboard correspond to each option on the screen and ‘Tab’ is used to go back and for ‘End Turn’. These numbers are clearly visible on each button. Keep an eye on the Action Panel in the top-left corner.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/8b32b2935eda427de681433fd237bf7c96ad50d1.gif[/img]

[h2]Game Speed Hotkeys[/h2]

The Game Speed can be changed using Hotkeys. The ‘<' button reduces the speed whereas '>’ increases it. Continuously tapping just one of these buttons also allows the speed to be cycled back. Keep an eye on the Game Speed in the top-right corner.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/1adaf738c99735b45796f15b13068b288f941710.gif[/img]

[h2]Menu Hotkeys[/h2]

Pages and tabs in different menus can be changed with Hotkeys. Different menus have different tabs/pages so the controls differ for each one. This information is always reflected in the bottom bar.

notes.title: Crimson Tactics Devlog #082
notes.content:
Crimson Tactics is a tactical turn-based role-playing game. RPG’s are complex games that can have a steep learning curve and are not immediately easy for players. These modes give new players a choice to play on an easier difficulty in order to acclimatize themselves to games of this genre, if they wish to do so.

[h2]Game Modes[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/392fcab5910cbe6a81e09fd14779c66222e3f697.png[/img]

[h3]Strategy Mode[/h3]

Strategy Mode is the original, intended method of play. The game is harder with more enemies and slower movement. It is meant for genre veterans and players used to tactical, turn-based RPGs.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/6f2cba285ff7b038833ee36bd6562c5c37fd8ef2.png[/img]

[h3]Tactics Mode[/h3]

Tactics Mode is an alternative method of play. The game is easier with a smaller number of enemies and a higher range of movement. It is meant for newcomers to the genre and ease out the learning curve of the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/645698160f9c182d789fad618a41a70f769137fa.png[/img]

[h2]Difficulty Modes[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/3efb930ace4f45799b3fbb464c05ce36182a18f6.png[/img]

[h3]Automatic Difficulty[/h3]

This mode dynamically changes the difficulty during gameplay. It adjusts to your style of play and depending on how good you are, it poses a greater challenge. Again, the intended method of play.

[h3]Manual Difficulty[/h3]

This mode allows you to manually set a difficulty that will not change unless you change it through the Settings menu. This allows you to enjoy the game at your own leisure.

notes.title: Crimson Tactics Devlog #076
notes.content:
Defend is an action that you can take to ensure your units focus completely on defending and saves them from harm momentarily. But like anything in the heat of battle, it is not foolproof and can be exploited by intelligent enemies!

[h3]Action Panel[/h3]

A dedicated action called Defend has been added to the game. It is accessible from the Action Panel.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/e1309b894eaab7d4d745ca24edffcdf9a10f1cde.png[/img]

A unit must equip either a Shield or Tome in order to use it, which block physical and magical attacks respectively.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/940a9ff280e9d1a910e3ac57a5bb32728d283b74.png[/img]

[h3]Choosing Defend[/h3]

A unit uses one action per turn to use the Defend action. A unit cannot Defend if it uses long-range movement. It will block the first physical or magical attack that it receives but after that, the block is not guaranteed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/c947115a52e3ed1c76998ebe4646fa35c754ef03.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/2a0756c6aed244d48c4f3e8a2cad2bcf3b91ac71.gif[/img]

[h3]Executing Defend[/h3]

Using Defend will block the first Physical or Magical attack that the unit receives but after that, the block is not guaranteed. Also, if the unit uses Defend with a Shield, it is still susceptible to magical attacks and vice versa. In case this happens, Defend fails.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/5fe605a658f3e80c396bfa0619d1006c85d1da18.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/195b76c1448f6b0b7e9ba53b175505bcbb022f1d.gif[/img]

Necromancer units are summoners that can summon ghouls into battle - Skeleton, Phantom & Wraith. Their playstyle revolves around summoning the ghouls into battle and controlling them.

[h3]Skeletons[/h3]

notes.title: Crimson Tactics Devlog #070
notes.content:
[h2]Loyalty System[/h2]

The allegiance and devotion of the recruits towards their factions, leaders, or allies play an essential role in Crimson Tactics. Each unit's loyalty changes based on the player's choices and actions toward them.

[h3]Recruiting Enemy Units[/h3]

If a unit's Loyalty is high enough, it can recruit enemies in battles.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/7ea6ec8a5abc6b71573a16dcc9a4a7bee67e28a5.png[/img]

[h3]Recruitment Chance[/h3]

The player can see the chance of recruiting an enemy unit next to the damage preview

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/53c9b0537dedc667c1ce1b9bef6eb52b43f9af0b.png[/img]

[h3]Recruiting Enemy[/h3]

The ally unit talks and tries to manipulate and convince the enemy unit to join its cause.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/67057d6f6aba4a23926c4aaba16951049594c4f0.gif[/img]

[h2]Fleeing Mechanic[/h2]

Enemy units can flee losing battles depending on their current HP and Loyalty.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/fd2dd8739874f485e562a355406fa584dcc268e5.gif[/img]

The unit runs to the end of the map and escapes the battle to save itself from dying at the hands of the player.

notes.title: Crimson Tactics Devlog #069

Battle Arts are the special abilities of the Berserker class.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/c9462218d89f9113e57b167dbe020ccdf03de59c.gif[/img]

notes.title: Crimson Tactics Devlog #067
notes.content:
[h2]Potions[/h2]

Consumable potions can play an important role in a tactics game, as they can provide much-needed healing, buffs, remove debuffs, and provide other benefits to your units.

The player can use any potions that are available in the player's inventory through Inventory > Potions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/9188765f324985609617dacad45d2f55fb2418de.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/9333c7698b00a65d9505fc8cbe18b0b2e7d8d390.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/61dfa5ee88592be4af643935e7b0dde4dc8a9789.jpg[/img]

[h2]Types of Potions[/h2]

Here are some of the potions that are available to the player in the game:

[h3]Heal[/h3]

The player can use a Heal potion to regain some percentage of HP. The potion can be used on any unit including self.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/0d95edb4d7ff6f7badb87a1954e45b7f392d9461.gif[/img]

[h3]Revive[/h3]

The player can use a Revive potion to bring their incapacitated allies back to life.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/e6d148c3fe55c58aafe5124a31731b95694e51ff.gif[/img]

[h3]Replenish[/h3]

The player can use a Replenish potion to restore their MP or an ally's MP to cast powerful magic spells.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/bb3f50cf25f3146355692f03cf1c17be26b49b2f.gif[/img]

[h3]Antidote[/h3]

The player can use an Antidote on any unit to remove the Poisoned status effect.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/95875fd95f9b18e8a4eeb7e3ba1a59266f7b7d5d.gif[/img]

[h3]Max Heal[/h3]

The player can use a Max Heal potion on any unit or self to restore the HP back to 100%.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/d164b6cbaa4698f768680a57bea0933027e8c9d4.gif[/img]

notes.title: Crimson Tactics Devlog #066
notes.content:
[h2]AI Switching [/h2]

The player can switch to AI mode for friendly units through the action panel.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/2bb33990b043e8294bc1ec3d2ff41cc63394380a.png[/img]

[h2]Types of AI [/h2]

The player has a number of AI types to choose from, each of them following a different strategy to weaken the enemy side. It could be attacking from the front, infiltrating, or even flanking and kiting.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/abb50d423c43b687c4c36a9f9fc11881bccda64d.png[/img]

Here are some of the AI types explained:

[h3]Attacker[/h3]

These are the Frontline units that are aggressive attackers and are the driving force of the assault. They engage all the units they come across and are directed to kill.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/6ba5e5016ef98115c8009dc7af543097f94d60e3.gif[/img]

[h3]Ranged[/h3]

These units attack from a distance by kiting and flanking units. They find perch points and make good use of elevation to rain their attacks down on the enemy units from a safe location.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/ab37ab626edf51f7f3ee613d234ffd096dba9a56.gif[/img]

[h3]Rearguard[/h3]

These are the Defending units that are in charge of protecting vulnerable units (like priests, mages, etc) from incoming attackers. They do not actively engage the frontline and instead stay back and attack any incoming attackers.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/6960392e1cc6829a1d326da9a8cc86fdf370be96.gif[/img]

[h3]Support[/h3]

The Support units can heal, apply buffs, remove debuffs and keep the other squad members alive. They are highly vulnerable since their main task is to keep others alive and not use a lot of offensive abilities. It is highly recommended that these units hold the backline.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/2d5d043f82f79ce1003c40faf603d4995ea82294.gif[/img]

[h2]Interrupt AI [/h2]

The player can always pause the AI with the press of the 'Interrupt' button. The player can then disable the AI and regain control of any unit by selecting that unit and clicking the 'AI' button. The battle resumes as soon as the 'Resume' button is clicked.

notes.title: Crimson Tactics Devlog #059
notes.content:
Variability in playstyle is a hallmark of the combat system in Crimson Tactics. Your units are allowed to change their Classes as much as you desire. It is showcased here.

[h3]Accessing Class Change[/h3]

Class Change can be accessed through the Unit Condition screen of every unit found within the Party Management System.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/d5370b7ebc3c9fb887b9058d7e7309395d6d4e98.gif[/img]

[h3]Changing Class[/h3]

In order to change your unit's Class, you must first acquire a 'Class Mark' for that Class. This is the currency required to change classes and can be found across the Shops in Wendalle or after battles as loot.

You must select the Class you want to change the unit to via the carousel where you can view various bits of relevant information such as Attributes and Usable Gear.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/deec4713b5f5450064982792ed3ce0c24d5ab5bb.gif[/img]

[h3]Class Stat Changes[/h3]

Every Class has certain basic Stats that it inherently possesses. As units level up, they gain stats based on that Class's traits. However, if a unit changes its Class, its Base Stats change even though the stats it gained on leveling up remain.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/12e1f59c5950898a23b0d21ae2e9a33d1897d119.png[/img]

notes.title: Crimson Tactics Devlog #057
notes.content:
The ability to Block is an important part of any battle. Units will block incoming attacks in two different ways based on whether they are Physical or Magical attacks.

[h3]Shield Block[/h3]

All Physical attacks - Melee or Ranged - can be blocked using a trusted Shield. Shields must be equipped in the Off-Hand slot in order to use them.

A Shield's usage will depend on its Block Chance and the unit's own Agility (AGL) stat.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/4068cd751792480cce92101844e69972b9aadb0b.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/d9036b153609b4777be8d58ff5bd1ef34e3fa984.gif[/img]

[h3]Tome Block[/h3]

All Magical attacks - Spell Casts or Abilities - can be blocked using a Tome. Tomes are special defensive spellbooks used by Mages across Wendalle to defend them and their allies from incoming magical projectiles. Tomes must also be equipped in the Off-Hand slot in order to use them.

A Tome's usage will also depend on its Block Chance and the unit's own Agility (AGL) stat.

notes.title: Crimson Tactics Devlog #055
notes.content:
Magic in the game is offensively cast as ranged single-tile or area of effect spells that can either buff, debuff or damage one or many targets. These spells must be learned by finding spell books known as 'Grimoires' throughout the game world, teaching them and assigning them to units.

The Magic Management menu can be accessed via the Unit Details screen which can be found through the Party Management or Party Deployment screens. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/51e7424b0d0020c8971181dbee189829cbdd8704.gif[/img]

[h3]Learning Magic[/h3]

Upon selecting ‘Learn’, a panel opens up that shows the available Grimoires. Units can only learns spells that are the same element as their Elemental Affinities.

Filters are available that divide all the magic as per the Elemental Affinities.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/d078336293f3d8748b31c5aefb5de4d0ebb377b8.gif[/img]

[h3]Assigning Magic[/h3]

After learning magic spells, they must be assigned to the unit so that they can actually use it in battle. Since every unit has a maximum of 5 slots available, the player must choose which element or elements a unit will specialize in.

It also encourages the player to have multiple units who can wield magic.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/2c0cdd6128f93a68b1e54960de47e79a6a556e19.gif[/img]

The details of each Magic Spell is available in a panel that appears on hovering over the buttons.

notes.title: Crimson Tactics Devlog #043
notes.content:
There will be many locations in Crimson Tactics that will have waterbodies - some shallow, some deep. Gameplay and visuals will change when these geographical features are present in different locations.

[h2]Shallow Water[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/c3dc45927cb021b8b5ae3856d88c357c84d2ab61.gif[/img]

All characters can move around in Shallow Water. Their feet will be slightly submerged in the water and their accuracy as well as agility will be somewhat decreased.

[h2]Deep Water[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/4a653711b5481f23da92468449dd89aa121dc2fe.gif[/img]

Characters cannot walk over Deep Water in normal circumstances. The only way to do is by applying the ‘Water Walk’ buff to characters. Characters that have used Water Walk will not have any part of their bodies submerged under the water, though their accuracy and agility will still be decreased.

[h2]Falling into Water[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/7e40f0b1778b76dd1c009e21bb9ca0802e2fe7be.gif[/img]

If characters are pushed onto a Deep Water tile and they do not have the Water Walk buff, they will immediately drown and be eliminated without any chance of being revived.

[b]PS[/b]: The Water in this particular level is all Shallow Water. Some tiles have been modified to demonstrate the Deep Water Gameplay.

notes.title: Crimson Tactics Devlog #030
notes.content:
There are 3 types of Character Units in Crimson Tactics:
[h2]Unique Character Units[/h2]
These units are significant characters in the game’s narrative, and the political thriller that is Crimson Tactics revolves around them.

[h3]Arlys Frink[/h3]
The protagonist of Crimson Tactics, Arlys is an able fighter and his actions will decide the fate of Wendalle. He can prove himself to be a capable leader or fail to save his own soul even, depending on what the player chooses.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/b22983a0f8485059e6fed55965371d096f13d815.png[/img]

[h3]Blazh Solberg[/h3]
Blazh’s life has been always affected by the turmoil eating away at his nation. It had finally forced him to take up his Bow and assist Arlys in his journey - becoming an ally and close friend.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/9a67e0095d07c411e95bf6ac1b84bdad0a0e0d08.png[/img]

[h3]Duke Beorn Rolfe[/h3]
Duke Beorn Rolfe comes from a line of royalty. An extremist and highly intelligent man, he usurps the throne of Wendalle from King Edrich Alwyn by allying with The Holy Empire of Asalia. He's a vicious, highly-skilled, two-handed Knight who can control Dark Magic - and can cut down squads of enemies without breaking a sweat.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/0b5461df5369cac0bee5c95fff9d71117c6d9fa3.png[/img]

[h3]King Edrich Alwyn[/h3]
King Edrich is the former ruler of Wendalle. He maintained peace throughout the kingdom using diplomacy and peaceful means. Unfortunately, his peaceful methods made him complacent and drew the ire of disruptive forces. He is slayed by Duke Beorn Rolfe, who had single-handedly sieged Castle White Pyre. His death throws the entire kingdom into turmoil and leads to an era of suspicion, duplicity, and betrayal.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/9010dc0d928388b2fd245cacc5f76e96afa9f6d2.png[/img]

[h2]Semi Unique Character Units[/h2]
Semi-Unique Characters are the supportive characters who help move the plot along and who may or may not serve as pawns in the larger political turmoil of Wendalle. 

[h3]Sir Unwin Braddock[/h3]
The Commander of the Knights under Duke Arsenio, Sir Unwin is a cruel and rough man who is defined by his corruption, greediness, and blind loyalty to the ruler of Swozalta, Duke Arsenio. His skill set as a fighter is great, only surpassed by his vanity as a commanding officer.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/9eeebacd568ce6e9a155c6209a0597de12ff355a.png[/img]

[h3]Rheda Solberg[/h3]
A kind-hearted, fiercely loyal ranger, Rheda is the agile and tenacious sister of Blazh. Her beauty is compounded by her resolve and her determination to see problems through. She loves her brother dearly and will do everything she can to protect him.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/542036b51fcc647cb06b530383bef7543c01fa90.png[/img]

[h3]Durwin The Deranged[/h3]
A powerful, if unhinged, warrior, Durwin got his nickname ‘The Deranged’ after he slew a party of men for spilling a drink on him at a pub. He’s bloodthirsty and merciless and respects nothing more than coin. He lives his life wanting nothing more than ale to drink, fights to pick, and skulls to crush.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/b26674244811c4efe60bd83ccaed8eb062b86fd1.png[/img]

notes.title: Crimson Tactics Devlog #026
notes.content:
[h2]AI Profiles & AI Protocols[/h2]
The AI System in Crimson Tactics is based on Nested Behavior Trees. Each unit has an [b]AI Profile[/b] which is a behavior tree. Each Node in the AI Profile is a separate Behavior Tree in itself. These nodes are called [b]AI Protocols[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/5c83494f259a8d014107f3f7353b957c9e57097f.png[/img]

[h2]Attack Nearest Unit Protocol[/h2]
Here is an example of an AI Protocol. This Protocol dictates the unit to seek out the nearest enemy unit and attack it. The behavior tree highlighted in green shows the selected branch of the tree and the corresponding action being executed by the AI.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/3cc2f714983a1ce63666dc2eb54e5a173cd142ca.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/f3cae5b7c1bfd794beff23924f9d77a3dc47cc48.gif[/img]

[h2]Behavior with different weapons[/h2]
The protocol works with both melee and ranged weapons. We can see the same basic attack protocol seeking out the nearest enemy and attacking it with a crossbow.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/e8ad5c453f56d877f543aa1ba9e43669c919d21a.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/565bead78fdd984d8403e49f2066715809d5e5bb.gif[/img]

[h2]Field Arts Protocol[/h2]
We also have Special Ability Protocols that make the unit execute Special Abilities. These Protocols are designed in a way to optimally use the stats of the unit.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/81852ead87271d36cb5f6b6fccb295e6d7fa320e.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/1408d8d7453eff30e0aaf1d6ad6b26d53a2ecce7.gif[/img]

[h2]Complex Behavior[/h2]
AI Protocols can be mixed and matched in the AI Profile to create complex behavior.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/a86b706491f9b70d5409e4db64ff53c2aa98912b.png[/img]

notes.title: Crimson Tactics Devlog #019
notes.content:
[h2]Crimson Tactics Spells[/h2]
Crimson Tactics features a full fledged Magic System. Moreover, each spell in the game can be cast in a variety of different ways.

[h3]Normal Cast[/h3]
This is the standard cast in the game. It deals 1x Damage, consumes 1x Mana and hits a single target.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/cdd8ca2e457a9bc980db226c360028a232326fb3.gif[/img]

[h3]Intense Cast[/h3]
Intense cast deals 1.5x Damage but consumes 2x Mana.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/d2d6c0c75be1f24e8c994aa64869af8a28fb9523.gif[/img]

[h3]Triple Cast[/h3]
A Triple Cast of a spell deals 0.67x Damage but is cast thrice and consumes 2x Mana. This is great for spells that have a low accuracy rate.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/9bc92b5d2c6c081804047d825118364ee4c82fbd.gif[/img]

[h3]Cross Cast[/h3]
A Cross Cast is a multi tile cast that deals 0.5x Damage to units in each tile and also consumes 2.5x Mana. This makes the spell an AOE attack.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/8eb470d02271ec3ff331f6d4356692dd40a8b0e6.gif[/img]

[h3]Block Cast[/h3]
Similar to the Cross Cast but this deals 0.67x Damage while consuming 2.5x Mana. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/b8e6a12519b65b35e2d5240a596da3bd4c499d15.gif[/img]

[h3]Philosopher's Cast[/h3]
The Philosopher's Cast is reminiscent of the Arithmetician class abilities from FFT. This cast allows the unit to deal damage based on different stats like WT, Elevation, Experience and Level, and the stats can be targeted using numbers (Prime, Multiples of 2, 3 and 5).
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/dd075edbae63a85d768741826ce6b59cad487a6c.gif[/img]

[b]Note[/b]: Damage and Mana Values are not final and are subject to balance changes. 

You can watch the Spell Cast Types in detail here:

[previewyoutube=tEK2ngqN-KY;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Crimson Tactics Devlog #014
notes.content:
[h2][b]Level Pipeline[/b][/h2]
This week we want to talk about how we make levels in Crimson Tactics.

[h3][b]Level Design[/b][/h3]
A Level Designer prototypes and designs a Rough Blockout of the Level. This also serves as the Simulation Layer for the Level.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/9050b3a3282f9345c3bd9674ec866e734ae894a5.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/1112ac1ecbbff70fe424c4c86522f9f364a6e8ae.png[/img]

[h3][b]Concept Art[/b][/h3]
Once the Level Design is done, a 2D Concept Artist decides the aesthetic of the Level and makes a 2D Concept.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/c16eae56a4fc336df5801777f27650cfae029dc5.png[/img]

[h3][b]3D Art[/b][/h3]
A 3D Art Team then takes the 2D Concept and makes it in 3D.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/2f8cbfb5b7e3d382e159fb59b690fd882befc2b1.png[/img]

[h3][b]Unity Render[/b][/h3]
The 3D Art is then imported into Unity and a Technical Artist tries to emulate the original vision of the Concept Art in Unity.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/19124332c2af5524698d63994442ec35de8fae23.gif[/img]

notes.title: Crimson Tactics Devlog #013
notes.content:
[h2][b]Character Pipeline[/b][/h2]
Last Devlog of the Year! In this Devlog, we are detailing our Character Pipeline while also revealing the Main Character of Crimson Tactics: The Rise of the White Banner.

[h3][b]Arlys Frink[/b][/h3]
[b]Age[/b]: 17
Of Swozaltan origin, Arlys hails from a family of thoroughbred knights revered for their loyalty and service to the Dukedom of Swozalta. Despite having lost the wise counsel of his father Ivan, to the civil unrest at Windsor, Arlys perseveres  to carry forth his father’s legacy by serving Duke Arsenio Duran.

However, a change of events led him to doubt his loyalties when he stumbled upon the Resistance of the White Banner. Alongside his new comrades Razia and Blazh, the ‘White Lion' now strives to put an end to the corrupt forces of Swozalta.

[h3][b]Concept Art[/b][/h3]
Our Character Pipeline starts with Concept Art. In this Phase, a 2D Artist works with a Narrative Designer to come up with a concept for the Character.

notes.title: Crimson Tactics Devlog #012
notes.content:
[h2]Cutscene Pipeline[/h2]
Merry Christmas!!! In this Devlog, we are detailing our Cutscene Pipeline.

[h3]Rough Outline[/h3]
The process of developing a Cutscene starts with a Narrative Designer writing the Rough Outline of the Scene. This is usually the first draft of the Scene and goes through many revisions before we settle on a final version.

[expand type=showmore]
The Duke enters the Throne Room and finally faces King Edrich. King Edrich had been waiting for him, mounted on Quvoss, and in his company are the remaining Royal Guards. Knowing his old friend and confidant, he knew that a fight was unavoidable but he needed to know what drove him to this extent. 

Edrich confronts Beorn and learns that Beorn  considers him a naïve and weak king for his pacifist ideals. Being an extremist, Beorn believes that an iron fist is what a ruler needs to bring order and unity to his nation- which he intends to, under the flag of the Holy Empire Asalia. Edrich realizes that Beorn is blinded by his own hatred, and so, he gives up hope of sparing his life.

The King orders his men to attack Duke Beorn. All by himself, Duke Beorn arms himself and charges towards them. Quvoss breathes fire at the Duke to stop him in his tracks and damage him but purple flames come from behind Duke Beorn at the right moment and nullifies Quvoss's white flames. Everyone looks behind Beorn. A Knight clad in black armor swoops in on a dragon of his own - a Hydra. The Dark Templars who assisted the Duke in the siege previously join in as well.
[/expand]

[h3]Story Fleshout[/h3]
After a Outline is approved, the Narrative Designer fleshes it out. The Dialogue is properly written and the events are more specifically described. At this point, the story is pretty much finalized. 

[expand type=showmore]
The Duke enters the Throne Room and finally faces King Edrich. King Edrich had been waiting for him, mounted on Quvoss. He is also accompanied by the last of the Guardian Knights. Knowing his old friend and confidant, he knew that a fight wasn't avoidable but he needed to know what drove him to this extent. Edrich confronts Duke Beorn.

“So, answer me.” the King demands calmly, “What madness makes you want to betray me? After all this time…after all that we’ve faced together, what makes you feel like stabbing me in the back?”

The Duke replies, “It’s not madness, my King. It's my love and loyalty towards my motherland. I cannot simply stand aside anymore and watch my people suffer.”

“Nonsense! Only a mad man would commit such sins! You will lead the people and the motherland you claim to love down a path of destruction. Because that is the only thing your new allies are capable of.”

“Do not be so conceited that you cannot see what this Kingdom needs. You are already leading it to ruin.”

“To ruin? Me? I have always been considerate of my people. I have always worked hard towards upholding my oath as a king, and you know it! You have been my friend and I have heeded your counsel numerous times. So, tell me, where does my kindness lack?”

“Your kindness is the reason why this kingdom is on the verge of breaking up into crumbs. Your naivety blinds you from the truth.”

“And what truth is that?”

“You cannot rule by making everyone happy. You cannot unite this kingdom with just kindness. A ruler needs a stern hand to unite his people. Your so-called kindness has only enabled the nobles’ infighting and divided the country into factions. I cannot let this continue!”

“Do not be so full of yourself! You think ruling with an iron hand will help you to unite people but it will never last. Because you can only make people follow you by winning their hearts. True unity can never be achieved with fear.”

“Winning their hearts?” Duke Beorn scoffs, “Feeding snakes do not make them lose their poison.”

“How can you govern a kingdom if you constantly doubt your subjects? In order to trust them and make them trust you, the only thing you can do is make their lives better by fulfilling their wishes.”

“Do not lecture me about trust. You do not even let foreigners enter this kingdom for trade for the fear of spies. Your misplaced trust and immature decisions have made this kingdom weak and prone to invasions.”

“Oh, but the people will be saved this time. And the kingdom will be united under the Holy Empire’s flag with me as the ruler.”

At the top we have the turn order carousel. The first unit is the unit whose current turn it is. Turn Order is not party based but instead based on a WT system that we will explain in a future devlog.

[h3]Actions Panel[/h3]
Below the Turn Order Carousel and on the left is the Actions Panel. This lists the actions available to the current unit. Right now only 3 options are shown but there will be a lot more in the actual game.

[h3]Tile and Weather Info Panel[/h3]
At the bottom right we have the Tile and Weather Info Panel. It shows the current tile's properties and the current weather conditions.

[h3]Unit Info Panel[/h3]
This panel shows the currently selected unit's information. It quickly shows the unit's Portrait, Allegiance, Name, Class, Level, Health Points, Mana Points, Battle Points, Status Conditions and Mount Status.

notes.title: Crimson Tactics Devlog #005
notes.content:
In Crimson Tactics, Dragons are part of the game's mounting system. Dragons serve as Tier 3 mounts which are the best mounts in the game. However, they occupy 4 tiles instead of 1. For short distances, Dragons just walk.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/18d490b1c485307bc2fa591f036784cfb7ca56d5.gif[/img]
For longer distances or for a difference in elevations, dragons will fly to their destinations.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40309613/207e85c281d9853e17c50bb158de1a879d4f88d1.gif[/img]

notes.title: Crimson Tactics Devlog #004
notes.content:
In Crimson Tactics, all in-game cutscenes will be rendered in isometric view. This is inspired from Tactics Ogre where they were able to convey a lot of emotions with just isometric cutscenes. In this cutscene, we show a soldier running away from a massacred battlefield. We wanted to capture the grim mood and convey what the soldier was feeling as he dashes across the massacred Courtyard.
